Logging._comment: Console is deliberately quiet so the ReviewProgressReporter's stage lines stand out (picked -> setup -> reviewing -> done). This filter is CONSOLE-ONLY; the opt-in JSONL sink (CodeReviewDaemon:LogFilePath) keeps full Debug detail for DuckDB. SingleLine collapses each entry to one readable line.

CodeReviewDaemon._comment_StrandedRun: A dropped PR resumes without a daemon restart (#317): StrandedRunReconciler sweeps on the poll's cadence and hands any non-terminal run back to the orchestrator once it has sat untouched past a window. There are TWO windows (#429): RetryPending — a retry the orchestrator deliberately asked for — gets the short one, and everything else gets the abandonment one. Both listings feed one pass and one resume cap. The knobs below are stated at their defaults so an operator can see and tune them rather than having to read the source to discover they exist.
CodeReviewDaemon._comment_StrandedRunGraceHours: Hours a non-terminal run must sit untouched before the reconciler takes it over. 0 disables the reconciler entirely. Must stay comfortably above ReviewStageDeadlineMinutes so a live run is never caught mid-stage.
CodeReviewDaemon._comment_StrandedRunScanLimit: Most stranded rows one pass READS from the store; rows beyond it are picked up by the following pass.
CodeReviewDaemon._comment_StrandedRunMaxResumesPerSweep: Most stranded runs one pass actually RESUMES. Deliberately small: a backlog built up over weeks must not become a burst of concurrent reviews — and, on a posting daemon, a burst of comments — the first time this runs. Deferred runs are logged, never dropped. Shared by BOTH listings below, so adding the fast path did not double it — and nothing is reserved for the slow listing, so a large enough retry-pending backlog delays genuinely stranded runs. That is bounded: settling a run re-stamps its updated_at, so it leaves the fast listing for a full fast window, and starving the slow listing at EVERY pass takes roughly (fast window / poll interval) x this cap — about 180 runs at the shipped defaults, not a handful. A starved run is deferred and logged, never dropped, and keeps its own StrandedRunGraceHours window.
CodeReviewDaemon._comment_StrandedRunRetryPendingGraceMin: Minutes a RetryPending run waits before the fast path resumes it, instead of the whole StrandedRunGraceHours window (#429). RetryPending is written deliberately by the orchestrator's stage catch — the run is OWED a retry — whereas Pending/Running only mean nobody has said anything, which is what an abandonment window is for. 0 switches the fast path off. Must stay comfortably above ReviewStageDeadlineMinutes (a live run stamps updated_at at stage boundaries, so a long stage looks untouched and would be resumed alongside itself) and below StrandedRunGraceHours (clamped if not). Lowering it is not free: this path resets the RetryGovernor, so the window IS the backoff and a permanently-broken run buys a full lease, clone and LLM run once per window.
